evals.prompt: Sketch construction-only Nautilus Rust 0.64.0 wiring for Databento data plus IB execution, with explicit typed configs supplied by the caller. Keep reconciliation enabled, risk bypass false, and do not start a connection. State what successful construction proves.
evals.expected_output: Native LiveNode factory/config routing with distinct data/execution routes, ending at build and stating qualification limits.
assertions: Uses native DatabentoDataClientConfig/Factory and InteractiveBrokersExecutionClientConfig/Factory with LiveNode.
Allows independent data and execution default routes, enables reconciliation and keeps risk bypass false.
Does not call start/run or discover credentials; construction does not prove account mode, entitlement or protective-order acceptance.

evals.prompt: My Nautilus live node started, Databento says connected, IB is on port 4002 and reconciliation is enabled. Mass status was missing but startup continued. May I admit new exposure? Explain the relevant Rust adapter evidence.
evals.expected_output: Withhold readiness claims until actual account, instruments, fresh data and sufficiently complete reports are demonstrated.
assertions: Missing mass status can warn and continue; enabled reconciliation is not proof of external state completeness.
Databento connections are lazy/local flags and need correct definitions plus fresh expected input.
Port 4002 alone does not establish a paper account or authorization.
Distinguishes IB report existence from completeness, including open-order/synthetic-position and execution/commission limitations.

evals.prompt: I only need an order-free Nautilus actor that computes a rolling indicator and emits custom data. No node, deployment or reconnection work. Which workflow should I use?
evals.expected_output: Choose building-nautilus-actors without expanding into live operations.
assertions: Routes to actor authoring and keeps the component order-free.
Does not introduce provider connections, secret discovery or infrastructure provisioning.
